newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch hotel puts euro on the menu.
newsitem.headline: Dutch hotel puts euro on the menu.

text.p: A Dutch hotel claimed on Friday to have produced the first full menu priced in euros, the planned new European single currency.

The Walkart Park restaurant at the Golden Tulip's Figi Hotel in Zeist in the central Netherlands offers its dishes priced in both guilders and euros, using an exchange rate of one euro to 2.16 guilders.

"We did this to start people thinking in a euro mentality -- just to make them aware of what they (euros) will be worth in Dutch guilders," spokesman Bart Maussen told Reuters, adding that the hotel management had itself fixed the exchange rate.

Maussen said diners had so far welcomed the new menu, which offers sauteed breast of pheasant with white cabbage at 39.50 guilders or 18.23 euros, a chocolate log and praline ice-cream with chocolate sauce for 14.50 guilders or 6.69 euros and wine from 42.50 guilders, or 19.62 euros, per bottle.

"They've been very positive. At first they were surprised and didn't know what the (euro) logo was for," he said. "Once it was explained to them, they said it was good and they should get used to it."
The Netherlands on Wednesday assumed the presidency of the European Union and one of its key tasks is to keep the 15-member bloc on track for monetary union.
The euro is due to become legal tender from January 1999.
